sentences.text: The genus Serpentisuchops contains only one species, S. pfisterae, named for Anna Pfister, the landowner where the holotype was found. Its generic name combines Latin words for snake and crocodile with a Greek word for face.
This medium-sized plesiosaur reaches over 7 meters in total body length and is unusual among derived plesiosaurs because it possesses both a long snout and a long neck.

The holotype specimen, GPM5001, was discovered at the Old Woman Anticline in 1995 and is now held by the Paleon Museum in Glenrock. The fossil material includes a partial skull, lower jaw, vertebral column, left ilium, and pubis.
The long snout of Serpentisuchops is likely an ancestral trait, while its long neck is a secondarily derived feature convergent with other groups.
The time range for Serpentisuchops is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
